objective_text: Explain concepts related to the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) reference model.
scope_summary: OSI layers 1 through 7 and the networking functions associated with each layer.

objective_text: Compare and contrast networking appliances, applications, and functions.
scope_summary: Physical and virtual routers, switches, firewalls, IDS/IPS, load balancers, proxies, NAS, SAN, wireless APs and controllers, CDNs, VPNs, QoS, and TTL.

objective_text: Summarize cloud concepts and connectivity options.
scope_summary: NFV, VPCs, security groups and lists, cloud gateways, VPN and direct connectivity, deployment and service models, scalability, elasticity, and multitenancy.

objective_text: Explain common networking ports, protocols, services, and traffic types.
scope_summary: Common ports and services, IP protocol types including TCP, UDP, ICMP, GRE, and IPsec, plus unicast, multicast, anycast, and broadcast traffic.

objective_text: Compare and contrast transmission media and transceivers.
scope_summary: Wireless and wired media, fiber types, copper and coaxial cabling, cable speeds and ratings, transceiver protocols and form factors, and connector types.

objective_text: Compare and contrast network topologies, architectures, and types.
scope_summary: Mesh, hybrid, star or hub-and-spoke, spine-and-leaf, point-to-point, three-tier, collapsed-core designs, and north-south versus east-west traffic.

objective_text: Given a scenario, use appropriate IPv4 network addressing.
scope_summary: Public and private addressing, APIPA, RFC1918, loopback, subnetting, VLSM, CIDR, and IPv4 address classes.

objective_text: Summarize evolving use cases for modern network environments.
scope_summary: SDN, SD-WAN, VXLAN, data-center interconnects, Zero Trust, SASE and SSE, infrastructure as code, source control, and IPv6 transition methods.

objective_text: Explain characteristics of routing technologies.
scope_summary: Static and dynamic routing, BGP, EIGRP, OSPF, route selection, NAT, PAT, FHRP, virtual IPs, and subinterfaces.

objective_text: Given a scenario, configure switching technologies and features.
scope_summary: VLAN databases and SVIs, native and voice VLANs, 802.1Q tagging, link aggregation, speed and duplex, spanning tree, MTU, and jumbo frames.

objective_text: Given a scenario, select and configure wireless devices and technologies.
scope_summary: Channels and widths, frequency bands, band steering, SSID identifiers, wireless network types, WPA2 and WPA3, guest access, authentication, antennas, and AP modes.

objective_text: Explain important factors of physical installations.
scope_summary: IDF and MDF placement, racks, airflow, patching and fiber panels, physical locks, UPS and PDU considerations, power load, voltage, humidity, fire suppression, and temperature.

objective_text: Explain the purpose of organizational processes and procedures.
scope_summary: Physical and logical documentation, inventories, IPAM, SLAs, wireless surveys, lifecycle management, change management, and configuration baselines.

objective_text: Given a scenario, use network monitoring technologies.
scope_summary: SNMP, flow data, packet capture, baselines, anomaly alerts, log aggregation, SIEM, API integration, port mirroring, discovery, traffic analysis, and availability and configuration monitoring.

objective_text: Explain disaster recovery (DR) concepts.
scope_summary: RPO, RTO, MTTR, MTBF, cold, warm, and hot sites, active-active and active-passive availability, tabletop exercises, and validation testing.

objective_text: Given a scenario, implement IPv4 and IPv6 network services.
scope_summary: DHCP configuration and relay, SLAAC, DNS security and record types, zones and resolver roles, hosts files, NTP, PTP, and NTS.

objective_text: Compare and contrast network access and management methods.
scope_summary: Site-to-site and client-to-site VPNs, clientless access, split and full tunneling, SSH, GUI, API, console, jump hosts, and in-band versus out-of-band management.

objective_text: Explain the importance of basic network security concepts.
scope_summary: Encryption, certificates and PKI, IAM, MFA, SSO, RADIUS, LDAP, SAML, TACACS+, authorization, least privilege, physical security, deception, risk terminology, compliance, and segmentation.

objective_text: Summarize various types of attacks and their impact to the network.
scope_summary: DoS and DDoS, VLAN hopping, MAC flooding, ARP and DNS poisoning or spoofing, rogue DHCP and APs, evil twins, on-path attacks, social engineering, and malware.

objective_text: Given a scenario, apply network security features, defense techniques, and solutions.
scope_summary: Device hardening, NAC, port security, 802.1X, MAC filtering, key management, ACLs, URL and content filtering, trusted and untrusted zones, and screened subnets.

objective_text: Explain the troubleshooting methodology.
scope_summary: Problem identification, theory development, theory testing, action planning, implementation or escalation, verification, preventive measures, and documentation.

objective_text: Given a scenario, troubleshoot common cabling and physical interface issues.
scope_summary: Incorrect media, signal degradation, termination and transmit-receive issues, interface counters and status, PoE faults, transceiver mismatch, and optical signal strength.

objective_text: Given a scenario, troubleshoot common issues with network services.
scope_summary: Spanning-tree loops and roles, VLAN assignment, ACLs, route selection, default routes, address pools, gateways, duplicate addresses, and subnet masks.

objective_text: Given a scenario, troubleshoot common performance issues.
scope_summary: Congestion, bottlenecks, bandwidth, throughput, latency, loss, jitter, wireless interference, channel overlap, signal degradation, coverage, disassociation, and roaming.

objective_text: Given a scenario, use the appropriate tool or protocol to solve networking issues.
scope_summary: Protocol analyzers, ping, traceroute, DNS tools, packet capture, interface and socket tools, Nmap, LLDP and CDP, speed testing, cable and optical tools, Wi-Fi analyzers, taps, and device show commands.
